{
  "summary": "Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files under a random or user-specified XOR key before loading the chainstate. File rewrites run sequentially in 1 MiB chunks using staged .reobfuscated files and directory commits to guarantee crash safety and resumability across restarts. Also logs a recommendation to reobfuscate when an unobfuscated blocks directory is detected and reports progress via kernel notifications.",
  "problem": "Nodes that synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with an all-zero XOR key, leaving them unobfuscated on disk. Node operators have no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate keys, or deliberately remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire blockchain.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing.'",
    "PR description benchmarks show single-threaded migration times ranging from ~10 minutes on an M4 Max NVMe SSD (854 GB) to ~24 hours on a Raspberry Pi 4B HDD (730 GB).",
    "References prior external/contrib work addressing the same user need: closed PR #32451 ('contrib: add xor-blocks tool to obfuscate blocks directory') and external utility andrewtoth/blocks-xor."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "Touches startup initialization, blockstorage file handling, filesystem helpers, and index DB constructors; adds functional test feature_reobfuscation.py.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Added canonical filename pattern matching for block and undo files (and staged files), preventing accidental staging/renaming of unrelated .reobfuscated files and correctly handling block/undo file numbers exceeding five digits in both migration and pruned reindexing.",
  "card": "Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option that rewrites existing block and undo files under a new random or specified XOR key without requiring a full resync. Nodes that initially synced before Bitcoin Core v28 store block files unobfuscated with a zero XOR key, leaving them susceptible to antivirus false-positives and without a native way to migrate or rotate keys. The migration operates sequentially using staged temporary files and directory fsyncs to ensure crash safety and automatic resumption upon restart. Progress is logged and broadcast to the GUI and RPC warmup via kernel notifications. Benchmarks report migration durations of roughly 10 minutes on fast NVMe SSDs to 24 hours on slow HDDs for full ~730 to 850 GB datadirs.",
  "needs": [],
  "confidence": "high",
  "uncertainties": [],
  "risk": {
    "level": "medium",
    "touches": [
      "validation",
      "other"
    ],
    "why": "A flaw in the staging, XOR application, or resume logic could corrupt block and undo files on disk, making historical blocks unreadable and requiring a full re-download of the blockchain."
  }
}

result.summary: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files under a random or user-specified XOR key before loading the chainstate. File rewrites run sequentially in 1 MiB chunks using staged .reobfuscated files and directory commits to guarantee crash safety and resumability across restarts. Also logs a recommendation to reobfuscate when an unobfuscated blocks directory is detected and reports progress via kernel notifications.
result.problem: Nodes that synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with an all-zero XOR key, leaving them unobfuscated on disk. Node operators have no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate keys, or deliberately remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire blockchain.
evidence: PR description: 'Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing.'
PR description benchmarks show single-threaded migration times ranging from ~10 minutes on an M4 Max NVMe SSD (854 GB) to ~24 hours on a Raspberry Pi 4B HDD (730 GB).
References prior external/contrib work addressing the same user need: closed PR #32451 ('contrib: add xor-blocks tool to obfuscate blocks directory') and external utility andrewtoth/blocks-xor.
result.scope_notes: Touches startup initialization, blockstorage file handling, filesystem helpers, and index DB constructors; adds functional test feature_reobfuscation.py.
result.changed_since_previous: Added canonical filename pattern matching for block and undo files (and staged files), preventing accidental staging/renaming of unrelated .reobfuscated files and correctly handling block/undo file numbers exceeding five digits in both migration and pruned reindexing.
result.card: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option that rewrites existing block and undo files under a new random or specified XOR key without requiring a full resync. Nodes that initially synced before Bitcoin Core v28 store block files unobfuscated with a zero XOR key, leaving them susceptible to antivirus false-positives and without a native way to migrate or rotate keys. The migration operates sequentially using staged temporary files and directory fsyncs to ensure crash safety and automatic resumption upon restart. Progress is logged and broadcast to the GUI and RPC warmup via kernel notifications. Benchmarks report migration durations of roughly 10 minutes on fast NVMe SSDs to 24 hours on slow HDDs for full ~730 to 850 GB datadirs.

risk.why: A flaw in the staging, XOR application, or resume logic could corrupt block and undo files on disk, making historical blocks unreadable and requiring a full re-download of the blockchain.
